facts.text: Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
Warren Buffett built his fortune by choosing companies with durable competitive advantages, predictable earnings, and management teams capable of allocating capital wisely.
Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.
But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase.
The Motley Fool Stock Advisor analyst team just identified what they believe are the 10 best stocks for investors to buy now… and Alphabet wasn't one of them.
If you're thinking about selling stocks to outrun a future bear market , let's look at wisdom from Warren Buffett.
His timeless advice should hopefully inspire the rest of us to avoid trying to "time the market."
No one knows if a bear market is really coming, or how long it will last, or when it will end, or how rapid the eventual recovery in the S&P 500 might be.
Even Warren Buffett himself frequently spoke humbly about how unpredictable and unknowable the day-to-day, month-to-month and year-to-year moves in stock market prices could be.
Here's the problem: timing the market doesn't work.
If you sell stocks right before a crash, you might miss out on the recovery.
The stocks you sell today might suddenly be more expensive when you're ready to buy back into the market.
You don't have to pick stocks like Warren Buffett to get rich.
From 1964 to 2024, Buffett earned a compound annual growth rate of about 19.9%.
Warren Buffett was a long-term investor who preferred to hold stocks “forever.”
Buffett has famously said that his favorite holding period (how long to wait to sell a stock after buying) was "forever."

Warren Buffett has carefully chosen how Berkshire Hathaway is positioned for the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution.
